method: 8 frames at 1,3,…,15 s; must-haves of V2/bench/mcp/flower/items/I94a.json; flower-judge (effort medium) per film; flower-pair (effort medium), random order; the same judge keyref-1 and keyref2 were scored with

case1.summary: Visually coherent widescreen naval footage preserves three crew and a binocular observation beat, but replaces the enclosed bridge with an open deck, misses the specified lookout and amber display, and does not establish the final fire command.

must_haves.item: The three crew match their descriptions and stay the same people throughout.
must_haves.why: The three people remain visually consistent; Vale has short dark hair, a dark naval coat and brass binoculars, and the foreground sailor has a blond braid, but her sleeves are not rolled and the male sailor wears a cap with no visible curly black hair or red headset.

must_haves.item: The bridge is a narrow steel bridge with slanted front windows, a chart table and cool overhead lamps, the same room throughout.
must_haves.why: The steel setting and chart table remain consistent, but this is an exposed deck with rigging and a mast, not an enclosed narrow bridge with slanted windows and cool overhead lamps.

must_haves.item: The actions happen in order: the lookout points at the horizon, Vale raises binoculars, then lowers them and gives the command to fire.
must_haves.why: The blond braided sailor, rather than the specified male lookout, points before Vale raises her binoculars; Vale briefly lowers them around 7 seconds but raises them again and still holds them up at 13 seconds, with no clear fire command established by the frames.

must_haves.item: A small tactical screen with amber graphics is visible on the bridge.
must_haves.why: A small console display is visible, but it shows a pale blue-green chart rather than amber tactical graphics; tracking the enemy vessel is not demonstrated.

must_haves.item: Cold late-afternoon light through the windows; about 15 seconds, widescreen 16:9; no extra people, no duplicated crew.
must_haves.why: The frames are 16:9, show cool overcast daylight and consistently contain only three crew without obvious duplication, but there are no windows; late-afternoon timing and the full 15-second duration cannot be verified from these samples.

v3-ship-1-s1-case3.summary: The consistent crew and convincing bridge largely match the visual brief, but the action order is wrong, the enemy appears as a translucent yacht-like overlay rather than a cruiser on the horizon, and the fire command is not verifiable.

must_haves.item: The three crew match their descriptions and stay the same people throughout.
must_haves.why: Vale has cropped dark hair, a navy double-breasted coat and brass binoculars; the lookout has curly black hair and a red headset; the helmsman has a blond braid and rolled sleeves visible early on. All three remain recognizably consistent.

must_haves.item: The bridge is narrow steel with slanted front windows, a chart table and cool overhead lamps, and remains the same room.
must_haves.why: The steel structure, angled windows, central chart table and cool ceiling lights are clearly established and maintained.

must_haves.item: The lookout points at the horizon, Vale raises binoculars, then lowers them and gives the command to fire.
must_haves.why: Vale raises the binoculars by 7 seconds, before the lookout's clearest pointing gesture at 9 seconds, and lowers them by 13 seconds. No clear fire command can be established from these stills, and no enemy cruiser is shown on the horizon.

must_haves.item: A small tactical screen with amber graphics is visible on the bridge.
must_haves.why: An amber-graphics screen is consistently visible behind the crew, although the frames do not establish that it tracks the vessel.

must_haves.item: Cold late-afternoon window light; about 15 seconds; widescreen 16:9; no extra people or duplicated crew.
must_haves.why: The frames show cold window light, approximately 16:9 framing and exactly three crew without duplicates. Late-afternoon timing and the full 15-second runtime cannot be independently confirmed from the supplied samples.

v3-ship-1-s1-case3 vs case1.why: The first video better matches the three crew descriptions and preserves the narrow steel bridge, slanted windows, chart table, cool lamps, and amber tactical screen. Although its pointing occurs after Vale raises her binoculars and an intrusive yacht overlay undermines the cruiser sighting, the second replaces the enclosed bridge with an open deck, omits the specified lookout appearance, and leaves Vale looking through binoculars at the end.
